title: Find the Duplicate Number
prompt:
`nums` has `n + 1` integers in the range `[1, n]`, so by pigeonhole at least one value repeats. Return the duplicate — **without modifying the array** and in **O(1) space**.

**Example**: `[1,3,4,2,2]` → `2`.

Why is this in the Linked List unit? Treat `i → nums[i]` as pointers: the duplicate value is where two indices point to the same node, i.e. a cycle entrance. Floyd's tortoise-and-hare finds it.
hints: Model the array as a linked list: index i links to index nums[i]. The repeated value is the node two links point into — a cycle entrance.
Phase 1: slow = nums[slow], fast = nums[nums[fast]] until they meet inside the cycle.
Phase 2: reset slow to 0; advance both by one until they meet — that's the entrance = the duplicate.

solution.explanation: O(n) time, O(1) space, array untouched. Values in [1, n] mean index 0 is never a target, so the functional graph from 0 must contain a cycle, and its entrance is the duplicated value — exactly the Linked List Cycle II algorithm applied to indices.
